data.name: Alee
data.gender_notes: Alee is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Alee is the name of several prominent figures in Islamic history, including the Prophet's cousin and companion, Ali ibn Abi Talib (ra). The name is derived from the Arabic root 'alaa', meaning 'to be high-ranking' or 'exalted'. In Islamic tradition, Alee is a symbol of spiritual excellence, wisdom, and courage. The name Alee carries the meaning “Exalted, Sublime” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Alee usually hope their child will grow to embody exalted, sublime and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Alee refers to Allah Almighty and denotes the one who is exalted and sublime, the greatest and the most powerful. It is a name of Allah and also of Prophet Ibrahim (as) and Prophet Zaid (ra).
data.etymology: Alee belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Exalted, Sublime.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Alee total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

The name embodies qualities of leadership, courage, and righteousness.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ali is deeply rooted in Islamic culture, particularly in the history of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and his companions. Ali ibn Abi Talib (ra) was a key figure in early Islam, serving as the fourth caliph and earning the title "Lion of Allah" due to his bravery and leadership qualities. The name Ali is also popularly used as a given name among Muslims around the world.

historical_references.reference: Caliph Ali ibn Abi Talib (656-661 AD) was the fourth caliph of Islam and a cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad. He was assassinated in Kufa, Iraq, during the Friday prayers in the mosque.
historical_references.context: Caliph and cousin of the Prophet Muhammad

historical_references.reference: Ali ibn Husain Zainabadi (1090-1156 AD) was a famous scholar, poet, and Sufi saint in the Islamic world. He is best known for his role in the Battle of Karbala and his famous speech during the mourning of Imam Husain (as), known as the Sermon of Zainab.
